title: Robert Pattinson chosen as the next James Bond | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

The name’s Pattinson,Robert Pattinson.

After months of intense rumors of acasting battle between some of the entertainment industry’s top names, actor Robert Pattinson, known for his roles in this year’s “The Odyssey” and “The Drama” — not to mention “Twilight” of years gone by — was announced as the next James Bond by Amazon MGM Studios viathe official 007 websiteMonday.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” the 40-year-old British actor said in a statement. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.”

The news of Pattinson’s casting was accompanied by ateaser clipof him as Bond — dressed, naturally, in a tuxedo and pointing a gun — as the series’ iconic theme song played.

Pattinson joins an elite club: Just six actors have portrayed 007. Sean Connery first appeared as the suave secret agent in 1962’s “Dr. No.” The most recent was Daniel Craig, who appeared as Bond in five films over 15 years, starting with 2006’s “Casino Royale” and most recently in 2021’s “No Time to Die.”

Production on the next Bond movie, the still-untitled 26th in the series, will begin soon under the direction of French-Canadian director Denis Villeneuve, who is also behind the “Dune” trilogy — the third installment of which costars Pattinson and comes out next month.

“We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007,” Villeneuve said in the statement, adding that Pattinson “has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new.”

To say that Pattinson has had a stellar year is an understatement. In addition to “The Drama” and “The Odyssey,” the actor is also courting awards buzz for his chilling portrayal of “To Catch a Predator” creator Chris Hansen in this fall’s “Primetime.” He’s also been filming as another legendary character, namely Bruce Wayne/Batman, in the upcoming “The Batman: Part II.” (“The Batman: Part II” comes from Warner Bros., which is owned by CNN’s parent company.)

Craig’s last turn as Bond in 2021’s “No Time to Die” ended with a closing credit promise that “James Bond will return.” Speculation over the next Bond simmered ever since. Yet for five years, Bond has been MIA while his corporate handlers went to battle.

In 2022, Amazon paid more than$8.56 billionfor Bond’s parent company, MGM, and thus the rights to distribute the 007 movies, but tensions soon emerged. Barbara Broccoli — who maintained creative control of the character thanks to a deal her late father, Albert “Cubby” Broccoli, had made with novelist Ian Fleming, the inventor of Bond — was reportedly highly distrustful of the data-driven Amazon, resulting in a standoff, according to a 2024 report in theWall Street Journal.

The impasse was broken a year later when a new deal was announced to finally hand creative control of the character to Amazon MGM Studios for an undisclosed sum, ending the Broccoli family’s control over 007 after more than 60 years.

After that, the hunt for the next Bond began gathering steam. Casting officially began inMay of this year,while second-round auditions were said to have been held inAugust.

Some of the biggest young stars in film were soon rumored to be in contention — although none were officially confirmed as potentials. Namesfloatedin thepressincluded Harris Dickinson, Callum Turner, Paul Mescal, Tom Holland, Jack Lowden, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Henry Cavill, Theo James and Jacob Elordi.

One major question long hung over the next Bond: was it time for 007 to be played by a man of color?

For years, fans of Idris Elba had championed him to play the next iteration of Bond, although as time went on the now-54-year-old actor seemed to age out of the role, especially given it would likely require stunt-heavy sequels.

Still, the names of otheryoungeractorswerefloated, including Dev Patel, Henry Golding, Regé-John Page and Daniel Kaluuya.

As casting continued, Elba seemed toshut down the idea of a non-white Bondas unrealistic and said the rumors around him were never based in truth. “James Bond was written how he was written for a reason,” Elba toldGQin June.

“In realistic terms, some markets just don’t go for that,” Elba said of a Black man playing 007. “Bond is big all over the world,” he said. “That’s not what they like in their culture. Period.”

No plot details or other casting for the next movie, based on a script from “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight, have been announced. It’s also not yet known if any actors from the previous films may return for what is widely expected to be a reboot of the series.
